payload.task_text:
You are a course analytics assistant for the Foundations of Finance course offered in Fall 2013. This course has a course ID of 16 in the learning management system.

Your task has three parts.

Part 1: Retrieve all assignments for course 16 and gather submission statistics for each one. For each assignment, collect the assignment name, total number of submissions, average score (rounded to 2 decimal places), number of late submissions, and late submission rate (late submissions divided by total submissions, multiplied by 100, rounded to 2 decimal places).

Part 2: Create a Google Forms survey titled "Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey" to collect student feedback on assignments. The survey must contain exactly 5 questions covering the following topics: overall assignment workload, clarity of assignment instructions, time required to complete assignments, availability of instructor support, and overall satisfaction with the assignments. Use appropriate question types for each.

Part 3: Create a Word document called Assignment_Analysis.docx in the workspace. The document must have the title "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis" at the top. It must contain a table with the following columns in this exact order: Assignment_Name, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score, Late_Submissions, Late_Rate(%). Sort the rows alphabetically by Assignment_Name. Include all assignments found in the course that have at least one submission (assignments with no submissions may be excluded).

After creating the Word document, send a summary email to instructor@financeou.example.com from analytics@university.example.com with the subject "Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)". The email body must mention the total number of assignments analyzed, the assignment with the highest average score, and the assignment with the most late submissions. Also include the Google Forms survey link in the email body.

The initial workspace contains Assignment_Guidelines.pdf for reference on the grading criteria used in this course.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently,

This is a compact one-course task. The main agent completes it directly; do not dispatch any sub-agent. Canvas is read-only.

First resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze it as `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. In one native-parallel response, call `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)`, extract all pages of `<workspace_root>/Assignment_Guidelines.pdf` read-only with `python_execute`, call `create_form(title="Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey")` exactly once, and search Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject. Select exactly one returned course whose code is `FFF-2013J` and whose full name is `Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)`; stop on zero or multiple matches, and never retry Form creation after an ambiguous result. Then call `canvas_list_assignments(course_id=<literal returned course ID>)` once.

From the returned assignment list, issue one independent `canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=<literal returned course ID>, assignment_id=<returned assignment ID>, page=1, per_page=1)` call per assignment in one native-parallel response. Use the whole-assignment `summary` returned on each call; do not page raw submissions. For every assignment with `summary.total_count>0`, compute:
`Total_Submissions=total_count`, `Avg_Score=round(avg_score,2)`, `Late_Submissions=late_count`, and `Late_Rate(%)=round(100*late_count/total_count,2)`.
Sort rows by exact assignment name. Select highest average score and most late submissions with assignment-name ascending tie-breaks.

Freeze one literal canonical payload containing all sorted rows, analyzed count, the two named extrema, and the verified Form ID/responder link. The Word document and email must consume exactly this payload without recomputing statistics.

Complete the Form chain on the retained ID, adding exactly these five multiple-choice questions in order and then reading the Form back:
1. `How would you rate the overall assignment workload?` — `Very light, Light, About right, Heavy, Very heavy`
2. `How clear were the assignment instructions?` — `Very unclear, Unclear, Neutral, Clear, Very clear`
3. `How much time did you typically spend on each assignment?` — `Less than 1 hour, 1-3 hours, 4-6 hours, 7-10 hours, More than 10 hours`
4. `How available was instructor support for assignments?` — `Never available, Rarely available, Sometimes available, Usually available, Always available`
5. `What is your overall satisfaction with the assignments?` — `1, 2, 3, 4, 5`
Require exactly this five-question sequence on the newly retained Form ID; do not append duplicates.

Create `<workspace_root>/Assignment_Analysis.docx` exactly once, preferably atomically with `python-docx`, using title `Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis` and one table with exact columns `Assignment_Name, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score, Late_Submissions, Late_Rate(%)`. Read the document back and require every canonical row in alphabetical order with literal numeric values.

For email idempotency, paginate `search_emails(query="Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)", folder="Sent", page=<n>, page_size=50)`, read every candidate, and match complete To, From, and Subject. Send exactly once only when no exact match exists, from `analytics@university.example.com` to `instructor@financeou.example.com`. The body must include canonical analyzed count, named highest-average assignment, named most-late assignment, and verified Form responder link. Repeat search/read-back and require exactly one exact message.

Accept only after the Form, Word file, and email read back against the same canonical payload.

nodes.text:
You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask, specify: (a) the dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore` (read-only), or `coder` (write-capable execution), and (b) whether the subtask is independent of its siblings (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output.

TASK CONTEXT:
- We are a course analytics assistant for the "Foundations of Finance" course, Fall 2013, with Canvas course ID 16.
- The workspace directory is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-assignment-feedback-gform-word/workspace and contains Assignment_Guidelines.pdf (reference only).
- Available tools: Canvas MCP (read assignments, submissions, grades), Google Forms MCP (create form, add questions), Word MCP (create/edit .docx), Email MCP (send email), local filesystem MCP, python execution.

TASK (3 parts):
Part 1: Retrieve ALL assignments for course 16 and gather submission statistics for each. For each assignment collect: assignment name, total number of submissions, average score (rounded to 2 decimals), number of late submissions, late submission rate (late/total*100, rounded to 2 decimals). Note: Canvas API list_assignment_submissions returns paginated results with summary totals and supports workflow_state='late' / late=true server-side filtering.

Part 2: Create a Google Forms survey titled "Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey" to collect student feedback on assignments. Must contain EXACTLY 5 questions covering: overall assignment workload, clarity of assignment instructions, time required to complete assignments, availability of instructor support, and overall satisfaction with the assignments. Use appropriate question types (e.g., multiple choice with Likert-style scales, or checkbox).

Part 3: Create Word document Assignment_Analysis.docx in the workspace. Title at top: "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis". Must contain a table with columns in EXACT order: Assignment_Name, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score, Late_Submissions, Late_Rate(%). Rows sorted alphabetically by Assignment_Name. Include all assignments with at least one submission (zero-submission assignments may be excluded).

Part 4 (final): Send a summary email to instructor@financeou.example.com from analytics@university.example.com, subject "Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)". Body must mention: total number of assignments analyzed, assignment with the highest average score, assignment with the most late submissions, and the Google Forms survey link.

DELIVERABLE: Return a numbered plan of subtasks with dispatch decisions (self/explore/coder), dependency/parallelism notes, and any verification steps you recommend (e.g., verify table contents after creation, verify form has exactly 5 questions, verify email sent). Keep it concise and actionable.
Plan task decomposition

You are a read-only exploration agent. Your job is to collect complete submission statistics for ALL assignments in Canvas course 16 ("Foundations of Finance", Fall 2013).

STEPS:
1. Call canvas_list_assignments(course_id=16) and record every assignment's id and name. (Expected ~13 assignments; if you see more, include all.)
2. For EACH assignment id, gather these statistics using the Canvas submissions API:
   a. TOTAL SUBMISSIONS: call canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=16, assignment_id=X, page=1, per_page=100). Page through (page=2, 3, ...) until pagination.has_more is false. The response includes summary totals — extract the total submission count and the average score from the summary (the summary covers the whole assignment even when paginated).
   b. AVERAGE SCORE: from the same summary totals (round not needed, just report the raw value).
   c. LATE SUBMISSIONS: call canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=16, assignment_id=X, page=1, per_page=100, late=true) (or workflow_state='late' if that parameter is supported) and count how many submissions are returned across all pages. If a server-side filter isn't honored, fall back to filtering the full paginated list yourself by checking each submission's late flag (submission.late == true) or workflow_state == 'late'.
3. Also record each assignment's points_possible if available (not strictly required).

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read-only: do NOT create, update, or delete anything. Do NOT send emails or create forms/documents.
- Do not access anything outside the Canvas API and the listed tools.

DELIVERABLE: Return a structured report, one line/entry per assignment, with fields: assignment_id, assignment_name, total_submissions, average_score (raw value), late_submissions. Note explicitly if any assignment has 0 submissions or if any API call failed (e.g., an assignment with no submissions may return an error or empty summary — record total_submissions=0 in that case). Report every assignment you found — do not skip any.
Collect assignment submission stats

You are a coder agent with access to the Google Forms MCP tools (mcp__google_forms__*). Your task: create a student feedback survey form.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Create a Google Form with EXACT title: "Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey". (Optionally add a description.)
2. The form must contain EXACTLY 5 questions, covering these topics:
   Q1: Overall assignment workload (e.g., "How would you rate the overall workload of the assignments?" — use a multiple choice Likert-style scale: Very Light / Light / Moderate / Heavy / Very Heavy)
   Q2: Clarity of assignment instructions (e.g., "How clear were the assignment instructions?" — multiple choice: Very Unclear / Unclear / Neutral / Clear / Very Clear)
   Q3: Time required to complete assignments (e.g., "How would you rate the time required to complete the assignments?" — multiple choice: Much Too Little / Too Little / About Right / Too Much / Much Too Much, or similar sensible options)
   Q4: Availability of instructor support (e.g., "How satisfied were you with the availability of instructor support?" — multiple choice: Very Dissatisfied / Dissatisfied / Neutral / Satisfied / Very Satisfied)
   Q5: Overall satisfaction with the assignments (e.g., "Overall, how satisfied are you with the assignments in this course?" — multiple choice: Very Dissatisfied / Dissatisfied / Neutral / Satisfied / Very Satisfied)
   Use the appropriate question type for each (multiple choice is appropriate for all five; a 5-point scale is recommended).
3. Mark questions as required if the API supports it.

TOOLS TO USE:
- mcp__google_forms__create_form (title, description) → returns formId
- mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question (formId, questionTitle, options, required)
- mcp__google_forms__get_form (formId) to verify

DELIVERABLE: After creating and verifying, return a concise report containing:
- The formId
- The exact form title
- The survey link / URL if available from the API response (look for a link/responderUri/url field in the create_form or get_form response)
- Confirmation that the form has exactly 5 questions with the topics above.
Create Google Forms survey
